messages.subject: DRUG today in PES 2005: Customizing your R Setup
messages.subject_clean: DRUG today in PES 2005: Customizing your R Setup
messages.body_plain:
See y'all in a bit!

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Noam Ross <noam...@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 30, 2012 at 12:55 PM
Subject: [D-RUG]: DRUG this week: Customizing .Rprofile
To: Davis R Users Group <davi...@googlegroups.com>

Hi all,

This week at at DRUG we will have a presentation from Ryan Peek on customizing your R setup:

> I [will] take 15 minutes to discuss how to customize your R startup and use Notepad++ or RStudio.  More specifically, I can discuss how to load sets of functions you may need frequently so they are available, as well as modifying several other options in your "Rprofile.site" file.

> I think it can also be helpful to discuss how to include a few lines of code in the top of your script to determine what computer you are working on (work, home, laptop, etc) which then sets a root file path, and then makes it easy to load file paths that may be slightly different across computers (I can also mention choose.file()/file.choose() in case folks aren't aware of it's use).

As a reminder, DRUG will on Friday, 10-12 in PES 2005.

Finally, we're looking for more presenters for future weeks!  Some possible topics below:

 - Best code organization practices (style guide)
 - Efficiency in coding - how to speed up your code
 - Version control (git)
 - Bayesian stats in R
 - Spatial analytics in R
 - Genetics/bioinformatics in R
 - Population modeling
 - Producing reports with knitr/sweave
 - Modeling admixture hybridization packages...
 - MCMC and the STAN package
 - Monte Carlo simulations in R
 - Interfacing with other languages (why and when?)
 - Working with LOTS of data more efficiently
 - Cluster computing and parallel processing

--
Check out our R resources at http://www.noamross.net/davis-r-users-group.html

>  - "Here's my problem" - take the group through what you're working on and soliciting feedback
>
> For "How to", I would encourage people to pick topics that they might not know a lot about, but would like to spend a bit of time collecting info and presenting resources (packages, tutorials, etc.)

> Here are some topics brought up at our first meeting that people might want to discuss:

messages.subject: Question on phylogenetically-controlled regression
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUG,

I have an analysis question I was hoping someone on the listserv could help me answer. I am trying to do a phylogenetically-controlled regression for a meta-analysis of Procellariiform seabirds. For each species included I have multiple measurements per species of the dependent variable (in this case, it's the proportion diet that is crustacea), but single measurements (thus no variance) for the independent variable (in this case it's the log-transformed weight of each species).

I have ran regular PGLS models <http://127.0.0.1:23742/library/caper/html/pgls.html> to control for phylogeny, but, I can only do so for each species mean y-value, thus leaving out a lot of data. I tried to use the recently published pgls.Ives function <http://127.0.0.1:23742/library/phytools/html/pgls.Ives.html>, to account for multiple measurements in the dependent variable, but I keep on receiving an error I don't understand.

If anyone works with these kinds of analyses and might be able to tell me what's going on, it would be greatly appreciated! Coped below, is my code and the associated data (.csv attached to this email).

Thanks in advance for your help!
Matt

My code for pgls.Ives model:
library(caper)
library(ape)
library(geiger)
library(phytools)

ProDataCrust <-read.csv("ProDataMeansCrust.csv", header = TRUE) # condensed .csv file with data (attached to this email)

#This is the code for the pruned phylogenetic tree I'm using for the analysis
tree = structure(list(edge = structure(c(19L, 20L, 21L, 22L, 23L, 23L,
24L, 24L, 25L, 26L, 26L, 27L, 27L, 25L, 22L, 28L, 29L, 30L, 31L,
31L, 32L, 32L, 30L, 29L, 28L, 21L, 20L, 33L, 33L, 34L, 34L, 19L,
35L, 35L, 20L, 21L, 22L, 23L, 1L, 24L, 2L, 25L, 26L, 3L, 27L,
4L, 5L, 6L, 28L, 29L, 30L, 31L, 7L, 32L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L,
13L, 33L, 14L, 34L, 15L, 16L, 35L, 17L, 18L), .Dim = c(34L, 2L
)), tip.label = c("Procellaria_aequinoctialis", "Halobaena_caerulea",
"Pachyptila_belcheri", "Pachyptila_salvini", "Pachyptila_desolata",
"Pachyptila_turtur", "Fulmarus_glacialoides", "Macronectes_giganteus",
"Macronectes_halli", "Daption_capense", "Thalassoica_antarctica",
"Pagodroma_nivea", "Pelecanoides_urinatrix", "Diomedea_exulans",
"Thalassarche_chrysostoma", "Thalassarche_melanophris", "Fregetta_tropica",
"Oceanites_oceanicus"), Nnode = 17L, node.label = c("Procellariidae",
"", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""
), edge.length = c(0.117647058823529, 0.176470588235294, 0.0588235294117647,
0.352941176470588, 0.294117647058824, 0.0588235294117647, 0.235294117647059,
0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.117647058823529, 0.0588235294117647,
0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.176470588235294, 0.352941176470588,
0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.117647058823529,
0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.176470588235294,
0.235294117647059, 0.294117647058824, 0.705882352941177, 0.764705882352941,
0.117647058823529, 0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647,
0.941176470588235, 0.0588235294117647, 0.0588235294117647)), .Names = c("edge",
"tip.label", "Nnode", "node.label", "edge.length"), class = "phylo", order = "cladewise")

# have to associate species names with values for pgls.Ives to process
X = ProDataCrust$log_wt
names(X) <-ProDataCrust$Binomial
y = ProDataCrust$prop_diet
names(y) <-ProDataCrust$Binomial
Vx = ProDataCrust$variance_log_wt
names(Vx) <-ProDataCrust$Binomial
Vy = ProDataCrust$variance_prop_diet
Cxy = cov(ProDataCrust$prop_diet,ProDataCrust$log_wt)

m1 = pgls.Ives(tree, X, y, Vx, Vy, Cxy) # Pro.tree.pruned.bl is the tree I downloaded from treeBASE and pruned for analysis, I can provide that for you too, if necessary

messages.subject: Paste Function Help!
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone--

I'm trying to do something that I imagine is very simple with the paste function. Specifically, I need to paste several text strings together separated by commas. The catch is that I need each string to be surrounded by quotation marks. For instance,

"blue" , "red" , "green"

The function paste("blue" , "," , "red" "," "green") results in "blue , red , green". I believe this has to do with escape characters, but I can't figure it out.

Thanks in advance!
--Mason

--
Mason Earles
PhD Student, Ecology Graduate Group
University of California - Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Paste Function Help!
messages.body_plain:
You can use single quotes as your "outer" quotes and doubles as your "inner", literal quotes:

> a <- paste('"blue"','"red"','"green"')
> a
[1] "\"blue\" \"red\" \"green\""
> cat(a)
"blue" "red" "green"

Note when you just type "a", this is equivalent to print(a), and this command adds the escape characters and quotes around the whole expression.  cat(a), on the other hand, prints the exact expression.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Increment operators like "+=" in R?
messages.body_plain:
R does not have an increment operator in base language, but it's implemented in the `Hmisc` package.  Instead of writing

    x <- x +1

you write

    inc(x) <- 1

The `dec` function does the same, but subtracts instead of adds.

messages.subject: DRUG this week: Population modeling
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This week at D-RUG we'll have a short presentation by Lauren Yamane on population modeling with R.  From Lauren:

> I will be discussing how to use R to generate a simple age-structured model with stochasticity that can be used to make plots of population time series.  If there's time, I can go into how to use R to evaluate the stability of a population by calculating and plotting the eigenvalues of the system.

See you Friday at 10AM in PES 2005,

Noam

messages.subject: New Course this Winter: Basics of data manipulation in R
messages.subject_clean: New Course this Winter: Basics of data manipulation in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Anna Steel is offering this great new course winter quarter for beginning R users.

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Anna Steel <annae...@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 26, 2012 at 1:12 PM
Subject: ECL298 - R for Dummies: Basics of data manipulation in R
To: Me <aestep...@ucdavis.edu>

ECL298 - Winter Quarter, 2013

Have you heard about ‘R’ but don’t have the slightest idea how to use it? Perhaps you’ve installed and opened the program, but keep getting frustrating error messages? Maybe you want to take an advanced course based in ‘R’ but need more familiarity with the code?

If so, then you’re in luck. Join us next quarter to master the basics of coding in R.

R is a powerful, flexible, open-source software for manipulating and analyzing data. It is constantly being improved and expanded by a diverse array of people. Many researchers claim it is the way of the future. We will spend ten weeks becoming comfortable with basic data manipulation in R. Everything from installing and setting up the program, to manipulating and sorting your data, to creating amazing plots, to becoming literate in the R-help dialect. If you already know a little, join us anyway! We will be flexible in our scheduling to account for different levels of experience.

The course will be offered Thursdays from 10:30 – 11:50, for 2 credits, S/U grading.

Please contact Anna Steel (aestep...@ucdavis.edu) for the CRN number

Interested and want to know more?

more details on WHAT: We are envisioning a ten week series that will cover the basic structure of R (what is object based coding?), how to read data into the program, to manipulate vectors and data frames, to write simple loops and functions, and to create and customize plots. We will also emphasize using built-in R-help files, approaches to troubleshooting, and useful R-coding ‘habits’.

more details on HOW: From personal experience, the best way to learn to use R is to, well, USE IT. But this can be endlessly frustrating as a new user without any assistance. Thus, the course will be structured to provide time for practicing new skills in class, with peers and other experienced R-users on hand to give feedback and trouble-shooting help. Each week a slide-cast will be posted for students to watch before class. This slide-cast will present new code, syntax, and/or functions which we will then apply to a dataset during our class time.

--
Anna Steel, PhD candidate
Biotelemetry Laboratory
Ecology Graduate Group
University of California, Davis

AnnaE...@gmail.com
